summary.name: HTTrack
summary.one_liner: HTTrack is a free, GPL-licensed offline browser that downloads a website to a local directory so it can be browsed offline, mirrored, or archived.
use_cases: Download a whole website for offline viewing
Mirror a website to a local directory
summary.what_it_does: HTTrack downloads a World Wide Web site from the Internet into a local directory, recursively building all directories and fetching HTML, images and other files. It rearranges the original relative link structure so the mirrored copy can be opened in a browser and navigated link to link as if online. It can update an existing mirror and resume interrupted downloads. The page says HTTrack is fully configurable and includes an integrated help system. Version 3.50 adds HTTPS support, files larger than 2 GB, Windows paths longer than 260 characters, and WARC output.
notable: WinHTTrack for Windows and WebHTTrack for macOS and Linux/Unix/BSD
Version 3.50 adds WARC output and HTTPS support
Updates existing mirrors and resumes interrupted downloads
caveats: WinHTTrack targets Windows 7 SP1 and later; Windows XP and Vista stop at version 3.49-2
The page does not detail limits of the mirroring process beyond the listed version changes
